account_sections.title: Why the 1888 death is probable
account_sections.markdown:
A death registered at **Gortahar on 16 May 1888** names an Alexander Glasgow. Is he the Lisnagaver farmer? Start with the apparent difficulty: the deceased was a labourer.

{{snippets:occupation}}

**The occupation change is compatible with this family.** Ann’s marriage already calls her father a labourer twelve years before the death. That weakens an objection to the match; it does not establish the deceased’s identity.

{{snippets:death-entry}}

**Now connect the places and relationships.** Alexander’s daughter Mary married Robert Elder. Later Elder records lead to Gortahar, and Mary Glasgow’s 1892 death names her daughter Mary Elder. This makes the 1888 death the best-supported located match, with an inferred final step:

{{visuals}}

**The 1888 informant reads Mary Glasgow, daughter.** That fits Alexander’s daughter Mary, who lived at Gortahar, although she was by then Mrs Elder. The register names neither a wife nor a former Lisnagaver address. [Read the complete comparison](#death-assessment).

### A real rival, not just a similar name

| Candidate | The useful comparison | Present conclusion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **This Alexander, Lisnagaver** | His daughter’s Elder family reaches Gortahar; “labourer” already appears in 1876. | Best located match; **probable**; the age conflict remains. |
| [Alexander of Glenleslie](/people/glasgow-2385.html) | Married Mary Anne Martin in [1847](https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1847/09322/5375567.pdf); the [1851 household](https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/census-record/#id=32216&census_year=1851) gives about **35**, implying about **72** in 1888, against the death age 84. | A genuine labourer namesake, **weaker but not excluded**. No located Gortahar or Elder link. |
| [Older Alexander](/people/glasgow-3904.html), estimated c.1770 | Would be about **118** in 1888 if the estimated birth is right. | No plausible claim on the present chronology; his own identity is reconstructed from tradition. |

The alleged **1882 death of the Glenleslie wife is unverified**. Even a verified death would require a remarriage check before the 1888 “married” status excluded her husband. The copied **1852 death** belongs to an unsupported Australian reconstruction; a DNA-project ancestor label repeating it is not a death record.

### Which Mary reported the death?

The forename was read as Nancy from 13 September to 6 October 2026. Compared with the same registrar’s other entries it reads Mary. Alexander’s daughter [Mary](/people/glasgow-3167.html) lived at Gortahar and is the natural candidate, but she had been Mrs Elder since 1871. She may have been entered under her maiden surname; the informant may have been Alexander’s wife Mary, with “daughter” written in error; or she may have been Mary Ellen Glasgow, born at Lisnagaver in 1867. Each belongs to this family. The local register original has not been viewed.

A burial or notice naming the deceased’s wife or former address would be especially useful. A proved death for Alexander-951 elsewhere, or a proved Glenleslie family at Gortahar with a daughter Mary, would challenge the match. [Full candidate comparison](#death-assessment).

account_sections.title: The case for John Glasgow
account_sections.markdown:
To look for Alexander’s parents, follow **Nancy Glasgow’s New York estate**. Her 1892 probate citation names James, Mary and Ann as children of Alexander, formerly of Rasharkin. Those names probably identify the family established above.

{{snippets:nancy-notice}}

**Start with Nancy’s own kin words.** The will names two relatives. Their Irish records supply the Glasgow mothers behind those names:

{{visuals:estate-links}}

**Now return to Alexander and John.** The probate citation places their children among the heirs. Combining that grouping with the will’s kin words and the Irish records supports a probable sibling network. It does not name Alexander’s father. The argument then uses John’s explicit father statement:

{{visuals}}

**The missing link:** no located record names Alexander’s father. Full siblings and half siblings have not been distinguished. The 1796 Desertoghill flax grower and the 1834 Robert Glasgow occupier remain separate, unproved identities. [Full parentage tests](#parentage-tests-2026-09-29).

### Could the early records require an older Alexander?

The **5 June 1829 Belfast News-Letter** extract reads:

> “Alex. Glasgow, Lisnagaver”

The alert and archive index derive from one occurrence. The [original page](https://www.newspapers.com/image/390582445/) was inspected **3 October 2026**: it lists **freehold applicant 2324**, with lands in **Kilconway barony, Lisnagaver townland**. The heading is now resolved. No age or kin is stated, and applying is not proof of admission. Alexander-951 and [older Alexander-3904](/people/glasgow-3904.html) remain compatible candidates.

{{visuals:early-ages}}

An adult qualification, if established, could affect the birth estimate or support a namesake. It would not automatically identify Alexander’s father. Using the probable death age to identify the 1829 man and then treating him as proof of that same death would be circular.

**1834:** Alexr Glasgow held 29 acres and Robt Glasgow 35 acres at Lisnagaver. Alexander could have been about 23; an older man is not required. Robert’s age and relationship are absent. **1836:** the field book’s house section names Robert and Archibald McCaughan junior; its land section supplies no occupier names. Alexander’s omission cannot establish co-residence or loss of a holding. [Tithe material](https://www.billmacafee.com/182030stithe/tithenorthantrimrevisionorder.pdf) · [Field book](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-994J-9HD6).

**Acreage cannot manufacture an inheritance.** The tithe uses Plantation measure; valuation uses statute measure. Lot 25’s 8 acres, 2 roods and 10 perches cannot be directly equated with the earlier 29 acres. [Land comparison](#record-account).

**Robert as a father is a separate identity test.** The indexed 1868 Robert death, age 71, implies birth c.1796–97. If he were the 1834 occupier, he would be only about **14–15** at Alexander’s c.1811 birth, or **7–8** under the earlier birth estimate. That weakens fatherhood conditional on the identification; it does not identify the occupier. [Death index](https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view/?record_id=cidenc-957324).


**1861:** the [Belfast News-Letter, 7 January, p.4](https://www.newspapers.com/image/387764534/) names Robt. Glasgow as a Lisnagaver neighbour who warned James M’Caughern before a house collapse. [Robert-938](/people/glasgow-938.html) and [Robert-3449](/people/glasgow-3449.html) remain compatible candidates. No age, kinship or connection to a valuation holding is supplied.

account_sections.title: The Irish–Canadian family
account_sections.markdown:
Canadian records now prove a sibling group linking **Kilrea, Lisnagaver and Prescott**. They expand Thomas and Daniel’s family, without yet making Alexander-951 another brother.

{{visuals}}

Robert’s [1849 will](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S) names his siblings. The [1861 deed](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWB8-D) identifies **Daniel, watchmaker of Kilrea, with wife Margaret**, and **Thomas, farmer of Lisnagaver, with wife Mary Anne**, selling the inherited two sixths. Their Irish identities are now established. The will does not call brother James deceased and names no parents.

### A father statement for a different Alexander

The [25 March 1868 deed, C114](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQRC-Y) identifies **Alexander Glasco, express agent of Rochester**, as son of **James Glasco, formerly of Prescott, carpenter**. Eliza Jane and Mary’s earlier deeds name that same carpenter as their father. These are three named children; no complete child count follows.

This is a concrete father statement. It belongs to the Rochester man. Applying it to Alexander-951 needs a wife, age, birthplace or migration bridge; none is established. The deed’s **18 August 1868** date is registration, not execution. [Power of attorney, C113](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQRK-B).

### The shares do not form a simple family count

{{visuals:shares}}

The daughters conveyed interests in the same parcels, but their deeds do not explicitly derive those ninths from Robert’s will. Additional ownership, inheritance or an error could explain the difference. The carpenter’s identity with Robert’s brother James remains a property-based hypothesis. Neither the fractions nor the common name selects Alexander-951’s father.

### Mary Glasgow Black’s six named children

The [15 September 1869 deed, C298](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQTY-K) expressly calls **Mary Black, formerly Mary Glasgow, Robert of Prescott’s sister**. It names a real family across three places:

{{visuals:black-children}}

Elizabeth had died unmarried and intestate; the five surviving siblings were her heirs. The deed subdivides **Mary’s one-sixth share** among her children. It names no parents for Mary and does not make her a daughter of Adam. Mary Glasgow Black is a different person from the carpenter’s daughter Mary Glasco of Rochester.

### Witnesses connect people, with identities still to prove

{{visuals:witnesses}}

The 1843 Black baptism transcription has a damaged mother’s name and “Thomson Black”. It cannot be changed to Thomasina without the original. A baptism date is also not automatically a birth date. [Black branch analysis](#black-witness-branch).

### Canadian leads that remain unassigned

The [estate index](https://www.ontariogenealogy.com/uppercanadaontariopioneerwillsestatefiles/leedsgrenvillecountieswillssurrogaterecords/leedsgrenvillecountieswillestateindex.html) has **Samuel Glasgow, 1875**, and **James E., 1900–09**. Younger Samuel-4021 and James E.-4017 are specific alternatives to older same-name relatives; these entries do not identify the merchant or carpenter. The [Niagara fonds](https://recherche-collection-search.bac-lac.gc.ca/eng/home/record?IdNumber=98738&app=fonandcol) concerns a farmer who died about 1830 and is excluded as the merchant’s archive.

The reported autosomal connection through Thomas’s daughter Catherine lacks a checked descent, shared-cM total and segment information in the supplied account. It remains a lead, with other shared-ancestor routes to test. [Full family and property analysis](#family-network).

account_sections.title: DNA and the Larne hypotheses
account_sections.eyebrow: 06 · Separate a paternal line from a pedigree
account_sections.markdown:
A tested descendant line of Alexander and a tested descendant line of **James J Glasgow** share **R-FT20271**. The historical men were not tested. The shared paternal ancestor remains unnamed.

{{visuals}}

### Three STR differences do not mean three generations

The maintained comparison gives **genetic distance 3 at Y-111**. STR mutations are uneven; this number does not identify a cousin degree or count father-to-son transmissions. Another line is closer on a larger callable Big Y STR panel, and the reviewed Block Tree contains no exclusive named downstream branch joining only Alexander and James J. [FTDNA explanation](https://blog.familytreedna.com/ftdnatip-report/) · [Wider DNA study](/ydna/).

### What the SNP evidence actually says

Historical names label descendant lines. **Derived** is a changed state; **ancestral** requires a reliable pre-mutation call. **Unresolved** is not an ancestral result. **Untested** means no SNP-level comparison in the supplied evidence.

| Descendant line labelled by historical ancestor | FT20271 | FT6135 | FTE32242 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Alexander-951 | Derived | **Ancestral** | Unresolved |
| James J-2738 | Derived | Unresolved | Unresolved |
| Reported William-591, c.1655; early pedigree unaudited | Derived | Unresolved | Unresolved |
| Reported Robert-12 through John M-1965 | Derived | **Derived** | Unresolved |
| Reported Robert-12 through William-563 | Derived | **Derived** | Unresolved |
| James M-193 through William Allen-2182 | Derived | Unresolved | **Derived** |
| James M-193 through Samuel Lyle-192 | Derived | Unresolved | **Derived** |
| Reported Robert of Kilwaughter-1143 · Y-111 only | Untested | Untested | Untested |
| Reported James of Kilwaughter-1144 · Y-37 only | Untested | Untested | Untested |
| Reported John of Inishrush-822 · Y-67 only | Untested | Untested | Untested |

Source: [public FTDNA project](https://www.familytreedna.com/public/Glasgow?iframe=ydna-results-overview), reviewed 13 September 2026, and the maintained August call audit. The private-call summary is not a separately reproducible public genotype dataset. Historical associations remain conditional on the supplied pedigrees. [Full dated matrix and provenance](#paternal-dna).

**The useful unresolved signal is FT6135:** Alexander’s audited result is ancestral; two reported Robert descendant lines are derived. That is a candidate grouping signal, not an established new branch. Resolve the James M son-lines and check the pedigrees before placing the mutation. A basal FT20271 display or a missing variants-file entry supplies no ancestral call. [SNP guidance](https://help.familytreedna.com/hc/en-us/articles/4402696079887-Big-Y-Matching-Matches-Guide).

### The American route has two missing relationships

{{visuals:american-route}}

Robert’s early-1790s birth fits Archibald’s under-ten boy in 1800; it does not name that boy. James-2439’s Newberry household is another age-compatible father candidate for James J. Compare its 1831 estate. James J’s [1848 Giles County deed](https://tngenweb.org/giles/deed-noah-hancock-to-james-glasgow/) proves residence then; its recital of an 1845 bond proves that transaction, not necessarily residence in 1845.

### Possible Irish routes now run through John Glasgow, farmer

James-1509 is a real **Larne ropemaker** in the [1760 ropewalk lease](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-S7XZ-8); a [1773 affidavit](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-M72W-M) says he was over thirty. His reported 1737 birth and proposed children require separate proof.

The estate argument makes **John Glasgow, farmer**, Alexander's probable father, so any Larne connection must join above John. The earlier routes through older Alexander-3904 and younger James-3986 each put a different man in John's place and are withdrawn as routes; they survive only as weaker rival fathers.

| Route above John Glasgow, farmer | How far it is supported | Missing evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hugh-1499 → John-4179 of Larne (married 1769) → John, farmer: the present WikiTree attachment | Possible, then unresolved: no record names John-4179's father or makes him John farmer's father. | A record naming John farmer's father. |
| James-1509, ropemaker → John, farmer | Unresolved; chronologically possible only. | The same. |
| William-1505 of Larne → John, farmer | Unresolved. The version through John of Glenleslie is disfavoured. | The same. |
| A County Londonderry origin (Desertoghill 1796; Tamlaght O'Crilly 1740) | Possible for the Desertoghill identity; unresolved above it. | Identity and parentage records for John. |

No record names John farmer's father, so the diagram cannot replace the missing records. [The routes in full](#larne-reconstruction).

**Chronology prevents an easy graft.** Adam’s estimated 1758 birth would make him only **12** at older Alexander’s estimated 1770 birth; Rose’s estimated 1767 birth would make her **3**. Changing dates or proposing an earlier mother adds unsupported conditions. James’s reported 1762 marriage to Janet Shutter also postdates Adam’s estimated birth, so Janet is not established as Adam’s mother.

William-3324 is a useful Larne-family comparison: his daughter Jane Shutter provides distinctive naming support. His **1815 will, D300/1/5/49**, is a concrete target. Reported STR lines through Robert-1143, James-1144 and John-822 need both SNP calls and audited descent before they can join the FT20271 comparison. [Complete Larne reconstruction](#larne-reconstruction).

account_sections.title: What could change the answer?
account_sections.markdown:
The useful checks target an identity or a relationship, rather than another nearby surname:

- **Nancy’s estate:** locate the actual 1894 appraisal and any surviving heir papers. The [original probate docket](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GYCZ-X98?view=fullText) records proceedings; it does not itself supply the missing relationships.
- **Mary Glasgow Thompson:** inspect the Scottish marriage original behind the new index lead, then establish whether that family belongs to Nancy’s Irish kin. It remains a separate, unproved identity.
- **The 1888 death:** view the local register original of the informant entry and compare the competing Alexander’s family records.

These checks can change the conclusion. Repeating the same family tradition or broad DNA match cannot. [Exact references and completed searches](#next-research).

**Other leads have limits:** the 1830 John Glassgow–McCaughern witness and the 1831 Black witness supply names, not kinship. The inspected 1829 freehold application could concern this man or an older namesake; registration records and qualification rules could help distinguish them. [Witness evidence](#john-glassgow-mccaughern-witness) · [1829 identity test](#record-account).

### The independent routes deserve equal attention

| Record to inspect | The identity or relationship it could test |
| --- | --- |
| Mary Thomson–Sneddon, 1860 Old Monkland marriage; [indexed mother Mary Glasgon Thomson](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6TLK-6T1K) | Original and later records could establish the mother’s parents or Irish origin. No link to Nancy is yet established. The differently aged Tannybrake widow is a separate candidate. |
| Ann McClelland’s own death and family records | Her sons’ records name **Ann Glasgow**, but her own parent statement would independently test the probable sibling network. |
| Robert’s Scottish birth-family records, 1869 and 1875 | Parents’ marriage date/place can test the bridge to **5 April 1866**. The reported 1902 death’s **644/2/849** citation must first be assigned to the right person. |
| Nancy’s 1894 appraisal and heir papers | The docket records a report filed **28 April 1894**, but does not reproduce its relationships or identify the special guardian’s ward. |
| Kilraughts–Dervock **CR5/32A/1**, c.1804–1831 | A household or family event could name Mary McCaughan’s parents. The manuscript is uninspected. |
| Pre-1858 probate name search and Larne succession | The later wills calendar cannot exhaust the earlier records. William’s 1815 will and Larne family material could test the joining generation. |

### Free newspaper routes now tested

News4Clues’s recommendations supplied two additional collections. Searches on **30 September 2026** found no new parent or sibling statement:

| Collection | What the searches established | Coverage and remaining gap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [HRVH Historical Newspapers](https://news.hrvh.org/veridian/) | Exact searches for **Nancy Glasgow / Glascow / Glasco / Glascoe** returned no hits. Alexander, John and Ann searches also returned none in the tested period. The 20 broad Nancy–Glasgow result snippets from 1850–1900 supplied no family match. | The [eight listed counties](https://news.hrvh.org/veridian/?a=p&p=regionbrowser) cover southeastern New York. **Plattsburgh and Rochester are outside that coverage**; reprints were possible, but this cannot close their newspaper routes. |
| [Sandusky District Library](https://www.sandusky.lib.mi.us/genealogy) | Exact **Minnie Boland** and **Minnie Glasgow** searches returned no hits. A cemetery entry for **Alex Glascow, 1842–1915**, is a different man. Exact **James Glasgow** returned one 1966 newspaper issue, whose wording remains unread. | This is a **Sanilac County** collection; the candidate James lived in **Tecumseh, Lenawee County**. The unread issue remains a lead, and a zero OCR result does not exclude a person. |

**The parentage conclusion is unchanged.** These searches refine the available routes; they do not weaken the Irish family reconstruction or prove the Michigan identity. [Exact terms, counts and inspection limits](#next-research).

### Read the claim at three different levels

{{visuals:method}}

An inaccessible original remains **uninspected**, not a negative search. An empty exact-name index result is bounded by spelling, indexing and coverage. Reprinted notices or copied family traditions do not become independent evidence by repetition. [Evidence method](#evidence-method) · [Precise references, outcomes and completed searches](#next-research).
